label: copy-phase input "t" (fed-back t, not the first copied token)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input token is t. It never fires on t during the original phase or at the delimiter, and never on any other input token. Every activation is a copy-phase t input (recall 1.0 for the predicate without the position condition). It mostly skips t when t was original token 0, i.e. t fed back at recall_idx 1, and is weaker or absent for t late in long sequences. Magnitude is largest when t was original token 1-2 (recall_idx 2-3, which carries about 65% of the mass) and in repeated t runs it drops for each later t. Top examples are around 0.9-1.0 of max at original position 2.

issues: The factual claims hold up. On the dev split all activation is in the copy phase (share 1.000) and in_tok is always t. Original and delimiter steps never fire, and the feature only fires when in_first=0. Without the position condition the test scores are precision 0.745 and recall 1.0, as stated. The full predicate reproduces on test: P 0.869, R 0.952, F1 0.909, mass recall 0.986.

The false positives are graded decay with position, not a clean class. Among copy-phase t steps, the share that fires is 0.193 at recall_idx 1, then 0.995, 0.982 and 0.955 at recall_idx 2, 3 and 4, then 0.767 at 5, 0.593 at 6 and 0.663 at 7+. Within recall_idx >= 5 it also falls with to_go (0.87 at to_go >= 3 down to 0.557 at to_go = 0). I found no token or history variable that splits these cleanly: digit count, vowel count, in_count and first_tok all leave the rate between 0.60 and 0.72.
Adding a cutoff for late positions does not help. '... & ~((recall_idx>=5) & (to_go==0))' gives P 0.924 but R 0.861, so test F1 drops to 0.891.
The missed activations are t that was original token 0, fed back at recall_idx 1. These are weak (about 0.01-0.16 of max) and hold 1.4% of the mass, which matches the explanation.

The run claim is a little overstated. 'Drops for each later t' holds in most top examples, but there are counterexamples, e.g. 'b t t e u j a a <DEL> b [t:0.72] [t:0.80]', where the second t is stronger.
The mass claim checks out: recall_idx 2-3 hold 0.322 + 0.333, about 65% of the activation mass.
